title: Milton Keynes City Council and Valon: streamlining planning with AI
summary: Milton Keynes reports faster validation and decisions during its Valon pilot, with receipt-to-validation time falling from 15.8 to 7.6 days.
account: Milton Keynes piloted Valon for planning work from October to December 2025. The council reports validation 60–80% faster. Register analysis showed receipt-to-validation decreasing from 15.8 to 7.6 days and validation-to-decision from 53.1 to 43.2 days. The 1,360 annual officer-hours figure is an extrapolation. Register comparisons do not isolate AI from other changes.
purpose: Support planning officers from application validation through decision-making.

ratings.reason: Faster validation and decision processing are reported time-saving gains.
Officers report less processing work, while register averages show shorter waits for applicants. These are convenience/time gains, not demonstrated improvements in decision quality.

ai_role.statement: The council used Valon in live planning work and reported shorter processing times. Timesheets and register data informed the estimates. The comparison does not isolate AI from other changes, and planning decisions remain officers’ responsibility.

evidence.citation: Local Government Association, AI case-study bank. Council or project account published by LGA. Hosting and editorial curation do not establish independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Milton Keynes City Council and Valon: streamlining planning with AI

produced_by: The pilot ran from October to December 2025 and used existing infrastructure.
The council collected timesheets and analyzed public planning-register data.
must_hold: The reported process keeps planning decisions with human officers.
The source does not establish which other conditions are necessary to reproduce the time savings.

headline: Milton Keynes reports faster planning validation with Valon
